key_insight: Entrance-induced vortices create geometry-dependent temperature-polarization bias whose magnitude and direction change with inlet Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: Lab-scale membrane characterization and heat-transfer correlations should account for inlet geometry and operating conditions rather than use a constant entrance correction.
method: Performed 3D CFD simulations of direct contact membrane distillation.
Varied inlet Reynolds number from 10 to 1000, side-chamber length, and main-channel height.
Compared temperature polarization with a straight-channel baseline.
evidence_signal: Across all simulated geometries, entrance vortices formed and persisted farther downstream at higher Reynolds numbers; most geometries shifted from stronger polarization than the baseline at low Reynolds numbers to weaker polarization at high Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation results but no experimental validation, so transfer to physical modules requires verification.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
